findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability in read_user_file
findings.description: The function allows a caller to specify arbitrary filenames, which can be used to read files outside the intended directory (e.g., by including "../"), because the input is not sanitized. This can expose sensitive data.
findings.reason: Confidence threshold met and supporting evidence provided.

evidence_references.explanation: User input is concatenated to the base directory without validation, permitting directory traversal.

findings.title: Command injection vulnerability in log_search
findings.description: The function concatenates user input into a shell command and executes it with shell=True, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary shell commands.
findings.reason: Confidence threshold met and supporting evidence provided.

evidence_references.explanation: User-provided query is directly concatenated into a shell command string, exposing command injection risk.
Using subprocess.check_output with shell=True executes the command string in a shell, which interprets metacharacters and allows injection.

findings.title: Insecure deserialization using pickle on untrusted data
findings.description: The function deserializes data received from an untrusted client using pickle.loads, which can execute arbitrary code and leads to severe security vulnerabilities.
findings.reason: Confidence threshold met and supporting evidence provided.

evidence_references.explanation: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle can execute arbitrary code, exposing the system to remote code execution attacks.
